transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~38m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Jin Park (Horizon Cloud - Head of AI), Aisha Khan (Horizon - CTO), Markus Li (Horizon - Infra Lead)

[00:00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um short intro from our side i'm samir, i run partnerships at redwood, with me is elena who is our solutions engineer
[00:00:10] Elena: hi all, excited to dig in, i'll be the technical lead on the call
[00:00:15] Jin: hey thanks, jin here, just to give context Horizon Cloud sells managed k8s + GPU instances to finance customers, exploring tighter integration with inference platforms, curious about hosting options and resale economics
[00:00:30] Aisha: yes we want to offer a bundled offering with GPUs + an inference runtime, rdr: regulatory customers ask for private deploy and audit logs
[00:00:40] Markus: infra constraints: multi-region (NA/EU), we need SSO, and we prefer to manage keys in our KMS, maybe HSM in future
[00:00:50] Samir: perfect, that's aligned with many of our partner conversations. quick high level: redwood provides hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc/on-prem) - same api surface across all. For partners we support reseller integrations and co-managed private deployments.
[00:01:10] Jin: can you explain the difference between dedicated and private? we've seen vendors use both terms inconsistently
[00:01:20] Elena: yeah, good Q. dedicated is reserved capacity in redwood's infra - think of it as predictable throughput with capacity reservation but still on our control plane. private means the control plane can be customer-managed or in a VPC - data plane stays local to your network, keys in your KMS. Some customers run our private package on-prem.
[00:01:45] Jin: ok makes sense. how about latency numbers - our customers expect sub-200ms p99 for small prompts (~64 tokens) for reranking workflows
[00:01:56] Elena: depending on model, hardware and our kernel selection you can see p50s in 20-40ms and p95/p99 can vary. With dedicated GPU pools and warm KV caching we can hit sub-200ms p99 for 64-token workloads on optimized models. we'll send a benchmark template so you can map to your GPU profiles.
[00:02:20] Markus: what is KV cache? i've heard of prefix caching but not sure how it interacts with multi-tenant GPUs
[00:02:28] Elena: KV-cache is our key-value attention cache that persists activations between request continuations; prefix caching stores common prompt prefixes so you avoid re-compute. For partners we provide guidance on memory sizing and eviction policies. In dedicated/private modes you can pin cache to tenants to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[00:02:50] Aisha: from compliance side we need SOC2, SAML/SSO support, audit logs, plus data residency for EU customers - how does that map to your offerings
[00:03:02] Samir: we have SOC2 and provide SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs; for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS and can support HSM-based key wrapping. For data residency we can run private in-target region or dedicated pools in region.
[00:03:20] Jin: great. commercial question: if we resell do we need revenue share or is there a flat partner fee?
[00:03:28] Samir: partner program is flexible - we do rev-share for resellers and also offer committed capacity discounts for co-sell deals. i'll send the partner deck with our tiers and example pricing.
[00:03:45] Jin: perfect. technical follow-up: we run benchmarks on V100 and A100 instances; we also have clients on a new accelerator (custom SOC) - how easy is model compatibility?
[00:03:58] Elena: we onboard models at the compilation and kernel-selection layer. most open models work out of box; for custom accelerators we may need to validate kernel ops. For GPUs you should be fine - we also support quantized variants. if you have a specific model list i can take a look.
[00:04:20] Markus: lock in question: do you require data to leave our VPC in private deployments?
[00:04:26] Elena: no, in private mode the control plane can be customer-managed; the data plane stays inside your network. there's an optional outbound telemetry channel for metrics that you can opt into.
[00:04:38] Aisha: latency vs cost tradeoffs - our customers vary, some are cost-sensitive, others need deterministic latency; how do you help partners tune those levers
[00:04:48] Samir: we expose batching, cache configs, quantization profiles, and routing policies. Redwood Optimize provides recommendations - e.g., batching vs no-batching heuristic for sub-100ms SLOs, and quantization for cost reductions. We can share anonymized case studies showing 2-3x cost improvement with minimal quality impact.
[00:05:10] Jin: any gotchas for Kubernetes-based resellers? we orchestrate GPUs with taints/tolerations and node pools
[00:05:18] Elena: integration points are usually the provisioning API and network plumbing. For private deployment we provide helm charts and an operator to manage model runtimes. We also integrate with your scheduler: you can map tenant workloads to node pools.
[00:05:35] Aisha: backups of models and audit retention - our legal needs 7 year audit logs for some customers, is that supported
[00:05:43] Samir: we can provide long-term log retention as an add-on and export to your SIEM. For model backups we support versioned artifacts in object stores.
[00:05:56] Jin: ok good. i'd like to run a small pilot - Horizon will provision 2 A100s in our EU region, we'd like you to run a short benchmark against a 7B and 13B model for token-generation and reranking. can you run that or provide a runbook?
[00:06:10] Elena: we can support both. two options: 1) we run benchmarks remotely against a dedicated pool that matches your GPU profile, or 2) we provide a benchmark runbook + spreadsheet and we run with your infra via a secure pipeline. Option 2 helps validate private deploys.
[00:06:30] Markus: security for option 2 - how do we share credentials for a limited window without exposing keys
[00:06:36] Elena: we use ephemeral credentials and recommend a short-lived service account with scoped permissions. We'll also sign an NDA as needed.
[00:06:46] Jin: sample timeline: pilot in 2-3 weeks, then eval with two enterprise customers to qualify the reseller offering within 2 months. Does that sound realistic?
[00:06:55] Samir: absolutely, that aligns - we'll aim for a tech deep dive next week and have materials ready for a pilot the week after.
[00:07:05] Markus: network egress costs are a big factor for us - if data leaves EU region costs spike; does private deployment avoid egress?
[00:07:14] Elena: yes private keeps traffic internal to region; for hosted options we'd recommend co-locating with your region and leveraging routing policies to avoid cross-region egress.
[00:07:26] Aisha: any reference partners in financial verticals?
[00:07:31] Samir: yes, we have a couple of banks and trading SaaS partners - i'll include anonymized benchmarks and reference architecture.
[00:07:38] Jin: what about observability and chargeback - we need token-level cost reports to bill customers
[00:07:44] Elena: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. For partners we can expose a billing API or CSV exports for chargeback.
[00:07:58] Samir: quick note - some transcription systems rename product names; don't be surprised if our internal doc says "Redwood Dedicate" i think the call transcription had that typo earlier
[00:08:05] Jin: (laughing) fair
[00:08:10] Elena: any blockers from your side for a pilot?
[00:08:14] Jin: procurement wants a standard MSA and data processing addendum; security needs SOC2 report and SAML + audit logs; infra wants a runbook and ephemeral creds w/ least privilege
[00:08:26] Samir: all standard - i'll get legal to share MSA/ DPA templates, and elena will share the runbook and benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:08:35] Aisha: do you support bringing your runtime as a container we can scan and run through our pipeline?
[00:08:42] Elena: yes we provide container images and helm charts for private deploy - we also publish SBOMs for scanning.
[00:08:50] Jin: about model licensing - some large models have license restrictions, do you handle licensing or is that on the partner
[00:08:57] Samir: we help with onboarding models and can surface license constraints; partners sometimes handle commercial licenses for proprietary models, but we have guidance and can broker where appropriate.
[00:09:10] Markus: can Redwood handle multi-tenant isolation at the runtime layer? we need strict tenant separation for audited workloads
[00:09:17] Elena: yes - tenancy isolation, KV cache pinning, per-tenant network policies, and cryptographic key separation are part of private/dedicated offerings.
[00:09:28] Jin: okay this is great - can you share a sample benchmark result so I can show the team what to expect?
[00:09:35] Elena: i'll attach a sample CSV and runbook, also a short video walkthrough.
[00:09:41] Samir: next steps recap: samir send partner deck + pricing, elena send benchmark spreadsheet + runbook + sample results, schedule se-led technical deep dive for 2026-09-18, horizon to share QPS/prompt distribution and compliance items.
[00:09:58] Aisha: thanks all, happy to proceed.
[00:10:02] Jin: thanks everyone

[00:10:10] --- (note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings) ---
[00:10:20] Speaker 2: so like if we do the private v p c, the logs are kept internal yeah?
[00:10:25] Elena: yes they're internal unless you opt into an export
[00:10:30] Speaker 1: can you do per-token billing?
[00:10:33] Samir: yep csv exports or api
[00:10:40] Speaker 3: what about inferencing on custom silicon?
[00:10:44] Elena: depends on op support, we can validate, often need a small porting effort

[00:11:00] (end of main call)
